literature.headline_zh: 尼帕病毒本期文献呈现多方向研究进展
literature.lead_zh: 本期尼帕病毒研究集中呈现以下进展。
key_findings_zh: 审查得出的结论是,NiV 暴发 仍然是流行地区的重大公共卫生威胁,由于缺乏获得许可的 抗病毒药物 或 疫苗,目前的管理层在很大程度上表示支持。它强调了单克隆抗体、抗病毒药物 药物(如瑞德西韦)和早期 疫苗 候选药物(重组蛋白、病毒 媒介 和 mRNA 平台)作为关键进展领域的有前途的临床前疗效。 [10.7860/jcdr/2026/87496.24264]
其中,随机森林模型表现出最高的预测性能,在训练(95%)和测试(86%)数据集上均实现了高精度。基于对接分数和分子动力学稳定性,我们确定了三个和五个有前途的候选物:2,3,4,5,6-五没食子酰葡萄糖、松果菊苷、Parishin A和新橙皮苷二氢查尔酮、柚皮苷二氢查尔酮、地奥司明、东荠菜素、阿米卡星,分别针对糖蛋白和RdRp。 [10.1007/s11030-026-11708-x]
尼帕病毒是一种能够在环境中生存和间接传播的包膜病毒,并且它仍然对常用的防腐剂和表面消毒剂敏感。 [10.1016/j.ajic.2026.06.003]
所有mAb均可中和NiV-M假病毒,但仅mAb A2可中和代表NiV孟加拉株(NiV-B)的假病毒。 [10.64898/2026.08.28.745669]
定性综合分析表明,尼帕病毒感染性高度依赖于标本基质效率和解剖学排毒模式。急性症状期呼吸道标本中病毒RNA拷贝数最高,与活跃的飞沫传播高度相关。 [10.1002/rmv.70194]

papers.title: Machine learning-driven drug repurposing and computational validation for Nipah virus.
papers.abstract: The recurring Nipah virus outbreaks and the lack of effective antiviral therapies, emphasize the urgent need for effective therapeutic interventions. Given the sporadic and unpredictable nature of NiV outbreaks, drug repurposing offers a time-efficient alternative to the development of novel antivirals. In this study, we leveraged machine learning (ML) techniques to accelerate the process of identifying potential therapeutic candidates. Several supervised ML models such as Support Vector Machines, Random Forest, Logistic Regression, Decision Tree, k-Nearest Neighbors, Artificial Neural Networks, and Ridge Classifier were implemented using publicly available NiV inhibitor datasets (viz. Anti-Nipah, NVIK, PubChem) as well as literature review (n = 211 compounds). Among these, the Random Forest model demonstrated highest predictive performance, achieving high accuracy on both training (95%) and testing (86%) datasets. papers.abstract_zh: 反复出现的 尼帕病毒 暴发 和缺乏有效的 抗病毒药物 疗法强调迫切需要有效的治疗干预措施。鉴于 NiV 暴发 的零星性和不可预测性,药物再利用为新型 抗病毒药物 的开发提供了一种省时的替代方案。在这项研究中,我们利用机器学习 (ML) 技术来加速识别潜在候选治疗药物的过程。使用公开可用的 NiV 抑制剂数据集(即 Anti-Nipah、NVIK、PubChem)以及文献综述(n = 211 种化合物)来实现多种监督 ML 模型,例如支持 媒介 机器、随机森林、逻辑回归、决策树、k 最近邻、人工神经网络和岭分类器。其中,随机森林模型表现出最高的预测性能,在训练(95%)和测试(86%)数据集上均实现了高精度。优化后的模型随后被应用于筛选 FDA 批准的临床前、临床和 抗病毒药物 药物库(包含 9021 种化合物),以识别潜在的抗 NiV 候选药物。入围的化合物通过分子对接进行了进一步验证,以评估结合亲和力,并通过分子动力学模拟来评估结构稳定性以及与关键病毒靶标的相互作用,包括糖蛋白和 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶 (RdRp)。基于对接分数和分子动力学稳定性,我们确定了三个和五个有前途的候选物:2,3,4,5,6-五没食子酰葡萄糖、松果菊苷、Parishin A和新橙皮苷二氢查尔酮、柚皮苷二氢查尔酮、地奥司明、东荠菜素、阿米卡星,分别针对糖蛋白和RdRp。这种综合方法结合了机器学习、药物再利用和计算验证,旨在加快发现针对 尼帕病毒 的有效治疗药物,并加强对未来 暴发 的准备。

papers.title: Nipah Virus Infection: A Narrative Review of Clinical Spectrum, Pathogenesis, and Emerging Preventive and Therapeutic Strategies
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is known to be an emerging zoonotic pathogen of the Paramyxoviridae family, which was first identified in 1998, and is also associated with high morbidity and mortality due to severe encephalitis and respiratory illness. Transmission occurs through direct contact with infected animals, contaminated food, and human-to-human transmission , thereby further highlighting its epidemic potential. Despite significant advances in understanding its virology, pathogenesis, as well as clinical manifestations, NiV outbreaks continue to pose substantial public health challenges, usually in endemic regions. Current management of NiV remains largely supportive with no licensed antivirals or vaccines available, thus emphasising the need for effective medical countermeasures. Recent therapeutic developments must focus on monoclonal antibodies and antiviral agents, including Remdesivir, which have shown promising efficacy in preclinical studies. Vaccine candidates, including recombinant protein, viral vector, and mRNA-based platforms, are being examined in their early phases of clinical evaluation, showing potential for robust protection of immunity. Future research priorities must include the development of rapid point-of-care diagnosis, strengthening genomic surveillance while also implementing One Health approaches integrating human, animal and environmental data for the prevention of spillover events. Refining animal models and elucidating immune correlates of protection are very important aspects for translating preclinical successes into adequately licensed interventions for management approaches for NiV. Collaborative international frameworks as well as structured R&D roadmaps are critical options for the acceleration of vaccine and therapeutic development, thereby further ensuring rapid deployment during outbreaks. This narrative review article highlights current knowledge on the epidemiology of NiV, pathogenesis, clinical management, as well as emerging preventive-therapeutic strategies while also identifying critical research gaps. It underscores the need for a proactive, integrated approach which combines medical, public health and scientific efforts for the mitigation of the threat of NiV globally.

analysis.scope_and_question: The review examines Nipah virus (NiV), a zoonotic paramyxovirus first identified in 1998, focusing on its clinical spectrum (severe encephalitis and respiratory illness), transmission routes (direct contact with infected animals, contaminated food, and human-to-human spread), and the central question of why NiV outbreaks continue to pose substantial public health challenges despite advances in virology and clinical understanding.
analysis.evidence_base_and_review_method: This is a narrative review that synthesizes current knowledge on NiV epidemiology, pathogenesis, clinical management, and emerging preventive-therapeutic strategies without conducting a systematic search or meta-analysis. The review does not report databases searched, eligibility criteria, study selection methods, or included-study counts.
analysis.consensus_and_key_conclusions: The review concludes that NiV outbreaks remain a significant public health threat in endemic regions, with current management being largely supportive due to the absence of licensed antivirals or vaccines. It highlights promising preclinical efficacy of monoclonal antibodies, antiviral agents like Remdesivir, and early-phase vaccine candidates (recombinant protein, viral vector, and mRNA platforms) as key areas of progress.
analysis.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review identifies critical gaps in translating preclinical successes into licensed interventions, including the need for refined animal models and elucidated immune correlates of protection. It also notes the lack of rapid point-of-care diagnostic tools and the insufficient integration of genomic surveillance and One Health approaches to prevent spillover events.
analysis.research_and_practice_implications: The review emphasizes the urgent need for developing rapid point-of-care diagnostics, strengthening genomic surveillance, and implementing One Health strategies to mitigate spillover risks. It also calls for collaborative international frameworks and structured R&D roadmaps to accelerate vaccine and therapeutic development and ensure rapid deployment during outbreaks.

analysis.summary_en: This narrative review synthesizes current knowledge on Nipah virus (NiV), a zoonotic paramyxovirus first identified in 1998, which causes severe encephalitis and respiratory illness. Transmission occurs through direct contact with infected animals, contaminated food, and human-to-human spread, contributing to its epidemic potential. Despite advances in virology and clinical understanding, NiV outbreaks remain a significant public health challenge in endemic regions. Current management is largely supportive, as no licensed antivirals or vaccines exist. Preclinical studies show promise for monoclonal antibodies, Remdesivir, and early-phase vaccine candidates (recombinant protein, viral vector, and mRNA platforms). Critical gaps include the lack of rapid diagnostics, insufficient immune correlates of protection, and limited translation of preclinical successes into licensed interventions. The review underscores the need for rapid point-of-care diagnostics, strengthened genomic surveillance, One Health approaches, and collaborative international frameworks to accelerate vaccine and therapeutic development and mitigate spillover risks.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,NiV 暴发 仍然是流行地区的重大公共卫生威胁,由于缺乏获得许可的 抗病毒药物 或 疫苗,目前的管理层在很大程度上表示支持。它强调了单克隆抗体、抗病毒药物 药物(如瑞德西韦)和早期 疫苗 候选药物(重组蛋白、病毒 媒介 和 mRNA 平台)作为关键进展领域的有前途的临床前疗效。

elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 该审查强调迫切需要开发快速护理点诊断、加强 基因组监测 并实施 One Health 战略以减轻 跨物种溢出 风险。它还呼吁建立国际合作框架和结构化研发路线图,以加速 疫苗 和治疗药物的开发,并确保 暴发 期间的快速部署。

papers.abstract_zh: 尼帕病毒 (NiV) 已知是副粘病毒科的一种新出现的人畜共患病原体,于 1998 年首次发现,并且由于严重的 脑炎 和呼吸道疾病,也与高发病率和 死亡率 相关。传播通过直接接触受感染的动物、受污染的食物以及人与人之间的传播发生,从而进一步凸显了其流行潜力。尽管在了解其病毒学、发病机制 以及临床表现方面取得了重大进展,但 NiV 暴发 仍然对公共卫生构成重大挑战,通常是在流行地区。目前 NiV 的管理在很大程度上仍然是支持性的,没有获得许可的 抗病毒药物 或 疫苗,因此强调需要采取有效的医疗对策。最近的治疗发展必须集中在单克隆抗体和 抗病毒药物 药物上,包括瑞德西韦,它们在临床前研究中显示出有希望的疗效。疫苗 候选药物,包括重组蛋白、病毒 媒介 和基于 mRNA 的平台,正在临床评估的早期阶段进行检查,显示出强大的免疫保护潜力。未来的研究重点必须包括开发快速护理点 诊断、加强 基因组监测,同时实施整合人类、动物和环境数据的“同一个健康”方法,以预防 跨物种溢出 事件。完善动物模型和阐明保护的免疫相关性是将临床前成功转化为获得充分许可的 NiV 管理方法干预措施的非常重要的方面。国际协作框架以及结构化研发路线图是加速 疫苗 和治疗开发的关键选择,从而进一步确保 暴发 期间的快速部署。这篇叙述性综述文章重点介绍了 NiV 的 流行病学、发病机制、临床管理以及新兴预防治疗策略的当前知识,同时还确定了关键的研究差距。它强调需要采取积极主动的综合方法,将医疗、公共卫生和科学努力结合起来,以减轻全球新病毒的威胁。

analysis_zh.scope_and_question: 该综述审查了 尼帕病毒 (NiV),这是一种于 1998 年首次发现的人畜共患副粘病毒,重点关注其临床谱(严重 脑炎 和呼吸道疾病)、传播 途径(直接接触受感染动物、受污染的食物和人与人之间传播),以及为什么尽管病毒学和临床取得了进展,NiV 暴发 仍继续对公共卫生构成重大挑战的核心问题理解。
analysis_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 这是一篇叙述性综述,综合了 NiV 流行病学、发病机制、临床管理和新兴预防治疗策略的当前知识,但未进行系统搜索或荟萃分析。该综述不报告检索的数据库、资格标准、研究选择方法或纳入研究计数。
analysis_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 审查得出的结论是,NiV 暴发 仍然是流行地区的重大公共卫生威胁,由于缺乏获得许可的 抗病毒药物 或 疫苗,目前的管理层在很大程度上表示支持。它强调了单克隆抗体、抗病毒药物 药物(如瑞德西韦)和早期 疫苗 候选药物(重组蛋白、病毒 媒介 和 mRNA 平台)作为关键进展领域的有前途的临床前疗效。

papers.title: Isolation and characterisation of Nipah virus neutralising candidate therapeutic monoclonal antibodies from an mRNA-immunised pig
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a highly pathogenic zoonotic paramyxovirus with epidemic potential. Despite the threat NiV poses, no therapeutics are licensed to treat infection. Studies have shown that monoclonal antibodies (mAb) can protect animals against NiV and the related Hendra virus (HeV). The best studied mAb, m102.4, has been used to treat infected patients on a compassionate basis, and has entered clinical trials. However, there is a need to define additional mAbs with therapeutic potential, which could be combined with m102.4 to improve neutralising potency and breadth. Here, we isolated five high affinity mAbs from an mRNA immunised pig, which bound the G glycoprotein derived from NiV Malaysia strain (NiV-M), and one of which (mAb A2) also bound HeV G. Aligned with this, all mAbs neutralised NiV-M pseudovirus but only mAb A2 neutralised pseudovirus representing the NiV Bangladesh (NiV-B) strain. mAb A2 and the most potent NiV-M neutralising mAb, C1, showed minimal competition with each other and m102.4, suggesting recognition of non-overlapping epitopes. Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy of the NiV-M G receptor binding domain complexed to A1 and C2 Fab fragments revealed distinct epitopes that did not overlap with the receptor-binding site, targeted by m102.4, suggesting action through steric impedance of receptor binding or interference downstream of receptor engagement. Inoculation of mAb A2 to hamsters did not provide complete protection against NiV-B challenge (60% survival), however, a split dose of mAb A2 and m102.4 provided the same protection as m102.4 alone (100% survival). Collectively, these data demonstrate the potential of the porcine model for isolation of therapeutic candidate mAbs, which contribute both to our understanding of the NiV G antigenic landscape, and the development of mAb combinations, that exert complementary mechanisms of neutralisation, for therapeutic intervention.

Aligned with this, all mAbs neutralised NiV-M pseudovirus but only mAb A2 neutralised pseudovirus representing the NiV Bangladesh (NiV-B) strain. mAb A2 and the most potent NiV-M neutralising mAb, C1, showed minimal competition with each other and m102.4, suggesting recognition of non-overlapping epitopes. Single-particle cryogenic electron microscopy of the NiV-M G receptor binding domain complexed to A1 and C2 Fab fragments revealed distinct epitopes that did not overlap with the receptor-binding site, targeted by m102.4, suggesting action through steric impedance of receptor binding or interference downstream of receptor engagement. Inoculation of mAb A2 to hamsters did not provide complete protection against NiV-B challenge (60% survival), however, a split dose of mAb A2 and m102.4 provided the same protection as m102.4 alone (100% survival). Collectively, these data demonstrate the potential of the porcine model for isolation of therapeutic candidate mAbs, which contribute both to our understanding of the NiV G antigenic landscape, and the development of mAb combinations, that exert complementary mechanisms of neutralisation, for therapeutic intervention.

analysis.research_question_and_background: The study aimed to address the knowledge gap regarding immune responses in bats to vaccines expressing antigens from Nipah virus and Ebola virus, as bats are hosts to diverse zoonotic viruses that can cause high case fatality rates in humans.
analysis.study_design_and_population: The study involved measuring antibody production and gene expression in two African bat species, Eidolon helvum and Epomophorus gambianus, following injection with vaccines encoding either a Nipah virus G glycoprotein or an Ebola virus GP glycoprotein.
analysis.methods: Using a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay and a pseudotype virus neutralization assay, the researchers observed an increase in antibodies against the Nipah glycoprotein in most bats that received the Nipah vaccine.
analysis.main_results: Transcriptomic analysis in Eidolon helvum revealed that genes involved in ISGylation and T-cell differentiation pathways were differentially expressed in response to the Ebola, but not the Nipah, vaccine.
analysis.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate species-specific differences in responses to antigen exposure, offering insights into bat adaptive immune systems and providing calibration for serological data from wild bats.
analysis.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform surveillance strategies and improve the interpretation of serological data from wild bat populations, which is critical for understanding zoonotic transmission risks.
analysis.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on two bat species and the absence of in vivo immunological studies, but the evidence is strong due to the direct observation of antibody responses and transcriptomic changes.

analysis.summary_en: This study investigated the immune responses of two African bat species, Eidolon helvum and Epomophorus gambianus, to vaccines expressing antigens from Nipah virus and Ebola virus. The researchers used a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay and a pseudotype virus neutralization assay to measure antibody production and gene expression changes. They observed an increase in antibodies against the Nipah glycoprotein in most bats that received the Nipah vaccine, while only one bat species showed detectable antibodies against the Ebola glycoprotein. Transcriptomic analysis in Eidolon helvum revealed differential expression of genes involved in ISGylation and T-cell differentiation pathways in response to the Ebola vaccine. These results highlight species-specific immune responses to antigen exposure, providing insights into bat adaptive immune systems and aiding in the calibration of serological data from wild bats. The study's findings are significant for understanding zoonotic transmission risks and improving surveillance strategies. However, the study is limited by its focus on two bat species and the lack of in vivo immunological studies, which may affect the generalizability of the results.

elements_zh.study_design_and_population: 该研究涉及测量两种非洲蝙蝠(Eidolon helvum 和 Epomophorus gambianus)注射编码 尼帕病毒 G 糖蛋白或埃博拉病毒 GP 糖蛋白的 疫苗 后的抗体产生和基因表达。
elements_zh.methods: 使用基于 Luminex 的多重微球免疫测定和假型病毒中和测定,研究人员观察到大多数接受 Nipah 疫苗 的蝙蝠体内针对 Nipah 糖蛋白的抗体有所增加。
elements_zh.main_results: Eidolon helvum 的转录组分析显示,参与 ISGylation 和 T 细胞分化途径的基因在响应埃博拉病毒时存在差异表达,但在尼帕病毒 疫苗 中则没有差异表达。
elements_zh.interpretation_and_novelty: 结果证明了对抗原暴露反应的物种特异性差异,提供了对蝙蝠适应性免疫系统的见解,并为野生蝙蝠的血清学数据提供了校准。
elements_zh.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: 这些发现可以为 监测 策略提供信息,并改善对野生蝙蝠种群血清学数据的解释,这对于了解人畜共患 传播 风险至关重要。
elements_zh.limitations_and_evidence_strength: 该研究因其关注两种蝙蝠物种且缺乏体内免疫学研究而受到限制,但由于直接观察到抗体反应和转录组变化,证据是强有力的。

analysis_en.methods: Using a Luminex-based multiplex microsphere immunoassay and a pseudotype virus neutralization assay, the researchers observed an increase in antibodies against the Nipah glycoprotein in most bats that received the Nipah vaccine.
analysis_en.main_results: Transcriptomic analysis in Eidolon helvum revealed that genes involved in ISGylation and T-cell differentiation pathways were differentially expressed in response to the Ebola, but not the Nipah, vaccine.
analysis_en.interpretation_and_novelty: The results demonstrate species-specific differences in responses to antigen exposure, offering insights into bat adaptive immune systems and providing calibration for serological data from wild bats.
analysis_en.scientific_and_public_health_significanc: These findings can inform surveillance strategies and improve the interpretation of serological data from wild bat populations, which is critical for understanding zoonotic transmission risks.
analysis_en.limitations_and_evidence_strength: The study is limited by its focus on two bat species and the absence of in vivo immunological studies, but the evidence is strong due to the direct observation of antibody responses and transcriptomic changes.

papers.title: Pulmonary Histopathological Changes Associated with Nipah and Hendra Virus Infection: A Systematic Review
papers.abstract: Background: The Nipah virus and Hendra virus are zoonotic viruses from the Paramyxoviridae family, belonging to the Henipavirus genus. They are single-stranded negative-sense RNA viruses, highly virulent, classified at biosafety level 4, and currently lack specific vaccines or antiviral therapies. They present moderate lethality, which may reach higher levels during outbreaks. The incidence of these infections has increased due to environmental changes such as deforestation and degradation of natural habitats, bringing bats (natural reservoirs) closer to human-inhabited areas. In addition, cultural practices, such as the consumption of raw date palm sap and contaminated fruits, favor viral transmission to humans and animals. Transmission may occur through food contaminated by bat secretions, contact with infected animals, aerosols, and human-to-human spread. Clinically, these infections involve significant neurological and pulmonary impairment, potentially causing encephalitis, pulmonary edema, and severe respiratory inflammation, with lesions similar to those observed in COVID-19, requiring careful differential diagnosis. Therefore, the clinical, epidemiological, and public health relevance of this topic is evident, as well as the need for further scientific investigation of its pulmonary manifestations. Objective: To systematize the possible pulmonary histopathological changes associated with infection by Nipah and Hendra viruses. Method: This is a systematic review with a protocol registered in the Open Science Framework, conducted according to PRISMA recommendations. Searches (2000–2025) will be performed in Medline, PubMed, Cochrane, SciELO, Embase, and the Virtual Health Library, using a PECO-based strategy. Two independent reviewers will perform study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment using the RoB2 tool, with a third reviewer resolving disagreements. Studies involving animals exposed to Henipaviruses with pulmonary histopathological outcomes will be included. If sufficient data are available, a meta-analysis will be conducted using Odds Ratio (95% CI), a random-effects model, heterogeneity analysis (Cochran’s Q and I2), subgroup and sensitivity analyses, publication bias assessment (funnel plot and Egger’s test), and forest plot presentation using RevMan software. The certainty of evidence will be assessed using the GRADE system.

papers.title_zh: 尼帕病毒与亨德拉病毒感染相关的肺组织病理变化:系统性综述
papers.source_body_en: Background: The Nipah virus and Hendra virus are zoonotic viruses from the Paramyxoviridae family, belonging to the Henipavirus genus. They are single-stranded negative-sense RNA viruses, highly virulent, classified at biosafety level 4, and currently lack specific vaccines or antiviral therapies. They present moderate lethality, which may reach higher levels during outbreaks. The incidence of these infections has increased due to environmental changes such as deforestation and degradation of natural habitats, bringing bats (natural reservoirs) closer to human-inhabited areas. In addition, cultural practices, such as the consumption of raw date palm sap and contaminated fruits, favor viral transmission to humans and animals. Transmission may occur through food contaminated by bat secretions, contact with infected animals, aerosols, and human-to-human spread. Clinically, these infections involve significant neurological and pulmonary impairment, potentially causing encephalitis, pulmonary edema, and severe respiratory inflammation, with lesions similar to those observed in COVID-19, requiring careful differential diagnosis. Therefore, the clinical, epidemiological, and public health relevance of this topic is evident, as well as the need for further scientific investigation of its pulmonary manifestations. Objective: To systematize the possible pulmonary histopathological changes associated with infection by Nipah and Hendra viruses. Method: This is a systematic review with a protocol registered in the Open Science Framework, conducted according to PRISMA recommendations. Searches (2000–2025) will be performed in Medline, PubMed, Cochrane, SciELO, Embase, and the Virtual Health Library, using a PECO-based strategy. Two independent reviewers will perform study selection, data extraction, and risk of bias assessment using the RoB2 tool, with a third reviewer resolving disagreements. Studies involving animals exposed to Henipaviruses with pulmonary histopathological outcomes will be included. If sufficient data are available, a meta-analysis will be conducted using Odds Ratio (95% CI), a random-effects model, heterogeneity analysis (Cochran’s Q and I2), subgroup and sensitivity analyses, publication bias assessment (funnel plot and Egger’s test), and forest plot presentation using RevMan software. The certainty of evidence will be assessed using the GRADE system.

papers.title: Emerging infectious diseases (Mpox, Nipah, and Andes): A narrative review of transmission, environmental survival, and disinfection.
papers.abstract: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 尼帕病毒是一种能够在环境中生存和间接传播的包膜病毒,并且它仍然对常用的防腐剂和表面消毒剂敏感。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 该综述没有报告 尼帕病毒 谱系环境生存的比较数据,也没有具体量化针对 尼帕病毒 的消毒剂功效。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 强调快速识别尼帕病毒病例并严格遵守感染预防建议,以预防医院相关传播。

analysis_en.scope_and_question: The review examines Nipah virus (NiV), including NiV-Malaysia and NiV-Bangladesh lineages, focusing on its transmission dynamics, environmental survival, and susceptibility to disinfectants as they relate to nosocomial infection prevention.
analysis_en.evidence_base_and_review_method: This narrative review synthesizes epidemiology, clinical features, diagnosis, and treatment of Nipah virus with emphasis on environmental persistence and disinfection efficacy, using narrative synthesis rather than systematic methods.
analysis_en.consensus_and_key_conclusions: Nipah virus is an enveloped virus capable of environmental survival and indirect transmission, and it remains susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants.
analysis_en.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: The review does not report comparative data on environmental survival across Nipah virus lineages or quantify disinfectant efficacy against Nipah virus specifically.
analysis_en.research_and_practice_implications: Rapid identification of Nipah virus cases and strict adherence to infection prevention recommendations are emphasized to prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

papers.source_body_en: BACKGROUND: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus are emerging infectious diseases that cause outbreaks associated with nosocomial transmission. METHODS: This narrative review summarizes the Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus epidemiology, clinical manifestations, diagnosis, and treatment with a focus on environmental survival, susceptibility to antiseptics and disinfectants, and infection prevention. RESULTS: Mpox, Nipah virus, and Andes virus all survive in the environment and are capable of indirect transmission. All these viruses are enveloped and susceptible to commonly used antiseptics and surface disinfectants. CONCLUSIONS: Rapid identification of patients with known or suspected infections of these emerging viruses coupled with adherence to infection prevention recommendations will prevent healthcare-associated transmission.

papers.title: The Role of the Medical Laboratory in Identifying 'Super-Spreaders': Correlation Between Viral Load Kinetics and Human-to-Human Infectivity.
papers.abstract: Nipah virus (NiV) is a high-consequence zoonotic henipavirus characterised by severe encephalitis and respiratory distress, driving recurrent outbreaks with case fatality rates between 40% and 75% in India and Bangladesh. Within these outbreaks, 'super-spreading' dynamics play a critical role, where a small subset of individuals contributes to a disproportionately large share of secondary infections. To evaluate the relationship between human infectivity and viral load kinetics in Nipah virus infection and to define the role of the medical laboratory in identifying potential super-spreaders, a narrative review was conducted by executing a systematic search across PubMed, Scopus, and ScienceDirect for peer-reviewed literature published from 1998 to 2025. The qualitative synthesis demonstrated that NiV infectivity is highly dependent on specimen matrix efficiency and anatomical shedding patterns. Respiratory specimens yield the highest viral RNA copy numbers during the acute symptomatic phase, correlating strongly with active droplet transmission. Persistent real-time RT-PCR Cycle Threshold values below 25 (Ct < 25) in respiratory samples serve as an indirect laboratory indicator of high-risk shedders and should be interpreted alongside clinical and epidemiological findings. However, a comprehensive analysis indicates that super-spreading is inherently multifactorial. Early identification via frontline molecular diagnostics remains the cornerstone of breaking NiV transmission chains. Although a standalone viral load threshold is insufficient to predict a spreading event on its own, the medical laboratory provides an essential risk profile by combining longitudinal Ct kinetics with clinical and exposure data. Strengthening regional laboratory infrastructure and deploying standardized point-of-care molecular assays in endemic, resource-limited areas are urgent public health priorities.

elements_zh.scope_and_question: 本综述聚焦于尼帕病毒(NiV)感染与疾病,重点探讨病毒载量动态与人际传播感染性之间的关联。核心问题是医学实验室如何通过病毒载量分析识别潜在超级传播者,以及其对尼帕病毒防控的意义。
elements_zh.evidence_base_and_review_method: 本综述采用叙事综述方法,系统检索了1998年至2025年间在PubMed、Scopus及ScienceDirect发表的同行评审文献。纳入研究涵盖尼帕病毒传播性、病毒载量动态及分子诊断在识别超级传播者中的作用。
elements_zh.consensus_and_key_conclusions: 定性综合分析表明,尼帕病毒感染性高度依赖于标本基质效率和解剖学排毒模式。急性症状期呼吸道标本中病毒RNA拷贝数最高,与活跃的飞沫传播高度相关。
elements_zh.controversies_and_evidence_gaps: 全面分析显示,超级传播本质上是多因素的,单一因素(包括病毒载量)无法独立预测传播事件。综述强调需将纵向Ct动态与临床和流行病学数据整合,以实现准确的风险分层。
elements_zh.research_and_practice_implications: 加强区域实验室基础设施建设,在疫区资源有限地区部署标准化即时分子检测方法,是当务之急的公共卫生优先事项。医学实验室通过结合病毒载量数据与临床和暴露信息,为风险分层提供关键支撑。

papers.title: STRUCTURAL AND FUNCTIONAL INSIGHTS INTO THE REPLICASE/TRANSCRIPTASE SYSTEMS OF THE DEADLY BAT-BORNE HUMAN VIRUSES: MARBURG, EBOLA, AND NIPAH
papers.abstract: Replication and transcription of genomes in the human pathogenic viruses, viz. Marburg, Ebola and Nipah are accomplished by a virally encoded RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The enzyme performs this dual function with a polymerase cofactor, VP35, in Marburg and Ebola viruses and a phosphoprotein, P, in Nipah and its related viruses. As RdRp is indispensable for the viral lifecycle, it is one of the most attractive molecular targets for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics to control the spread of these viruses. However, until now, little is known about the RdRp of these viruses, especially with respect to their active sites, polymerase catalytic centre and its catalytic mechanism, which are considered the most promising molecular targets for drug development initiatives. In this study, multiple sequence alignment (MSA) was integrated with structural information from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and site-directed mutagenesis (SDM) studies to identify the putative catalytic and metal-binding sites of the RdRp from Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses. MSA analysis suggests that the RdRp from these viruses uses an -LA/VG- as the template-binding pair, an invariant K, as the proton abstractor which initiates the catalysis and an invariant R at -4 from the catalytic K, as the nucleotide discriminator, all of which are highly or completely conserved. Besides, the Marburg and Ebola viruses contain an additional second putative polymerase catalytic core within the N-terminal domain (NTD), which is absent in the Nipah virus polymerase. The identified catalytic residues exhibit strong structural similarity to the conserved polymerase catalytic site architectures already reported in numerous RNA- and DNA-dependent polymerases, supporting a common catalytic framework. The catalytic magnesium-binding sites are also completely conserved among these viruses and consist of two invariant aspartate-containing motifs, -GDN- and -TDL-. This arrangement differs slightly from that what is reported for several other non-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses, including influenza, rabies, mumps and measles, which typically use -GDN- and -G/SDD- motifs for catalytic magnesium-binding. Furthermore, the RdRp domains of all three viruses contain two putative zinc-binding motifs (ZBMs), suggesting an important structural role in polymerase stability and function. Interestingly, the RdRp of Marburg and Ebola viruses, members of the Filoviridae family, possess an additional putative HNH-endonuclease motif(s) that is absent in the Nipah virus polymerase, a member of the Paramyxoviridae family. Collectively, these findings reveal conserved structural and catalytic features of the polymerases from these bat-borne human pathogens, and provide new insights into their evolutionary relationships, and also identify potential molecular targets for rational antiviral drug design.

papers.title_zh: 致命蝙蝠源性人类病毒马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和尼帕病毒的复制/转录系统结构与功能洞察
papers.source_body_en: Replication and transcription of genomes in the human pathogenic viruses, viz. Marburg, Ebola and Nipah are accomplished by a virally encoded RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (RdRp). The enzyme performs this dual function with a polymerase cofactor, VP35, in Marburg and Ebola viruses and a phosphoprotein, P, in Nipah and its related viruses. As RdRp is indispensable for the viral lifecycle, it is one of the most attractive molecular targets for the development of broad-spectrum antiviral therapeutics to control the spread of these viruses. However, until now, little is known about the RdRp of these viruses, especially with respect to their active sites, polymerase catalytic centre and its catalytic mechanism, which are considered the most promising molecular targets for drug development initiatives. In this study, multiple sequence alignment (MSA) was integrated with structural information from X-ray crystallography, cryo-electron microscopy (cryo-EM) and site-directed mutagenesis (SDM) studies to identify the putative catalytic and metal-binding sites of the RdRp from Marburg, Ebola and Nipah viruses. MSA analysis suggests that the RdRp from these viruses uses an -LA/VG- as the template-binding pair, an invariant K, as the proton abstractor which initiates the catalysis and an invariant R at -4 from the catalytic K, as the nucleotide discriminator, all of which are highly or completely conserved. Besides, the Marburg and Ebola viruses contain an additional second putative polymerase catalytic core within the N-terminal domain (NTD), which is absent in the Nipah virus polymerase. The identified catalytic residues exhibit strong structural similarity to the conserved polymerase catalytic site architectures already reported in numerous RNA- and DNA-dependent polymerases, supporting a common catalytic framework. The catalytic magnesium-binding sites are also completely conserved among these viruses and consist of two invariant aspartate-containing motifs, -GDN- and -TDL-. This arrangement differs slightly from that what is reported for several other non-segmented negative-sense RNA viruses, including influenza, rabies, mumps and measles, which typically use -GDN- and -G/SDD- motifs for catalytic magnesium-binding. Furthermore, the RdRp domains of all three viruses contain two putative zinc-binding motifs (ZBMs), suggesting an important structural role in polymerase stability and function. Interestingly, the RdRp of Marburg and Ebola viruses, members of the Filoviridae family, possess an additional putative HNH-endonuclease motif(s) that is absent in the Nipah virus polymerase, a member of the Paramyxoviridae family. Collectively, these findings reveal conserved structural and catalytic features of the polymerases from these bat-borne human pathogens, and provide new insights into their evolutionary relationships, and also identify potential molecular targets for rational antiviral drug design.
papers.abstract_zh: 在人类致病病毒马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和尼帕病毒中,基因组 的复制和转录由病毒编码的 RNA 依赖性 RNA 聚合酶(RdRp)完成。该酶在马尔堡病毒和埃博拉病毒中与聚合酶辅因子 VP35 一起执行这种双重功能,在尼帕病毒及其相关病毒中则与磷酸蛋白 P 一起执行。由于 RdRp 对病毒生命周期至关重要,它是开发广谱 抗病毒药物 治疗药物以控制这些病毒传播的最有吸引力的分子靶标之一。然而,直到现在,人们对这些病毒的 RdRp 了解甚少,尤其是其活性位点、聚合酶催化中心及其催化机制,这些被认为是药物开发计划中最有前景的分子靶标。本研究整合了多序列比对(MSA)与来自 X 射线晶体学、冷冻电子显微镜(cryo-EM)和定点诱变(SDM)研究的结构信息,以识别马尔堡病毒、埃博拉病毒和 尼帕病毒 的 RdRp 的潜在催化和金属结合位点。MSA 分析表明,这些病毒的 RdRp 使用 -LA/VG- 作为模板结合对,一个不变的 K 作为质子抽取剂,启动催化反应,并且一个位于催化 K 前第 4 位的不变 R 作为核苷酸识别器,所有这些都高度或完全保守。此外,马尔堡病毒和埃博拉病毒在其 N 端结构域(NTD)中包含一个额外的潜在聚合酶催化核心,而 尼帕病毒 聚合酶则没有。所鉴定的催化残基在结构上与已报道的许多 RNA 和 DNA 依赖性聚合酶的保守催化位点架构高度相似,支持了一种共同的催化框架。催化镁结合位点在这些病毒中也完全保守,由两个不变的天冬氨酸含有的模体 -GDN- 和 -TDL- 组成。这种排列与其他一些非分节负链 RNA 病毒(如流感病毒、狂犬病毒、腮腺炎病毒和麻疹病毒)略有不同,这些病毒通常使用 -GDN- 和 -G/SDD- 模体进行催化镁结合。此外,所有三种病毒的 RdRp 域包含两个潜在的锌结合模体(ZBMs),这表明它们在聚合酶稳定性和功能中具有重要的结构作用。有趣的是,马尔堡病毒和埃博拉病毒的 RdRp,作为丝状病毒科的成员,还包含一个额外的潜在 HNH 核酸内切酶模体,而 尼帕病毒 聚合酶,作为副粘病毒科的成员,则没有该模体。总体而言,这些发现揭示了这些蝙蝠源性人类病原体的聚合酶在结构和催化方面的保守特征,并提供了关于它们进化关系的新见解,同时识别了潜在的分子靶标,用于理性设计 抗病毒药物 药物。
